title: The Information Dynamics of Insider Intent: How Reporting Inversions (Form 144) Mask Informational Rents in Insider Sales (Form 4)

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper investigates insider trading information dynamics using an event-study framework that links SEC Form 144 intent-to-sell notices to Form 4 trade executions. It uses a three-stage methodology combining univariate OLS baselines, a multi-paradigm predictive audit spanning linear models to deep neural transformers (such as FT-Transformers and XGBoost), and a causal machine learning ensemble including Double Machine Learning and Generalized Random Forests to estimate heterogeneous treatment effects on liquidity.
extraction.universe: 111,800 unique insiders across approximately 2.6 million matched transactions from LSEG Insider, BoardEx, CRSP, and Compustat

performance_metrics.context: Cumulative Market Excess Return (CMER) during the filing gap
Mean Cumulative Market Excess Return (CMER) during the filing gap
Paired t-test on the difference between CAR 144 and CAR 4

key_findings: A structural reporting inversion post-SOX means trade execution (Form 4) frequently precedes the notice of intent (Form 144), creating a persistent 52.4% opacity rate.
Unexecuted intent signals (aborted sales) remain statistically indistinguishable from routine executions within public datasets, establishing an information ceiling.
While small-cap portfolios yield higher absolute abnormal returns, statistically significant alpha is concentrated in large-cap firms due to higher institutional salience.
Causal machine learning confirms that aborted intent signals cause an illiquidity jump of up to 2.63 times at high-magnitude thresholds.
limitations: Data attrition occurs due to smaller companies lacking BoardEx coverage or sufficient CRSP history for factor calibration.
High-capacity machine learning models reach an asymptotic limit (PR-AUC ceiling near 0.40) due to unobservable idiosyncratic catalysts in the public feature space.
